column1: BOARD OF INTERMEDIATE AND SECONDARY EDUCATION GUJRANWALA
Board of Intermediate & Secondary Education, Gujranwala was established in 1982 with its jurisdiction over six districts i.e. Gujranwala, Gujrat, Hafizabad, Mandi Baha-ud-Din, Narowal and Sialkot,
under the Punjab Boards of Intermediate & Secondary Education Act 1976.
The Intermediate (First Annual) Examination 2025 commenced on 29-04-2025 and the written/theory papers ended on 13-06-2025. Total No. of candidates applied for admission to this Examination
were 138564.The result is being declared on 18-09-2025.
(i) This Result Gazette is issued as a notice only. Errors and Omissions are EXCEPTED. Any entry appearing in the notification does not independently confer any right or privilege to the candidates
for the grant of a certificate which will be issued in due course of time under the regulation.
(ii) The result of all candidates whether successful or otherwise is being published for convenience of all concerned.
(iii) The numerical figures given in the result column (Part I&II) show the marks obtained by the successful candidate while the abbreviations show the subjects in the result column of Part-I & II
gazette in which the candidate fails or any other position of the result.
2. CHANCE TO REAPPEAR FOR PART I & II (COMPOSITE)
(i) Who appeared in the Intermediate First Annual Examination 2025 in full subjects and absent without the condition to pass minimum number of subjects, shall have three consecutive chances to
appear in failing subjects till Intermediate Second Annual Examination 2026. iii)      Who appeared in the Intermediate First Annual Examination 2025 and failed to qualify the failing subjects shall
have to repeat the Examination as a whole under part system in the Forth Coming Examination.
This time, successful efforts have been made to reduce the number of result later cases to negligible percentage. However, some results are pending of those who in spite of repeated reminders

As a result of strict measures adopted to curb the tendency of unfair means in the examination, a remarkable achievement has been noted. Despite of, vast and
comprehensive inspections only 19 cases in all could be detected with alleged use of unfair means in the Examination Halls. Their decisions have been made as under.
A judicious procedure has been observed to decide all these cases. Before deciding the cases of alleged use of unfair means fair opportunity of defence has been provided
to all the candidates involved in such cases. A liberal offer has been made to the candidates to avail the chance of personal interview with the discipline Committee and it has been
ensured that personal hearing is granted to every such candidate who has shown willingness for this purpose. All the undecided cases are pending for want of written reply from the
candidates in response to charge-sheet issued to them by the office. These candidates have been reminded more than once to submit their statements to the office to proceed
